france24fr.title: Liban : des habitants inspectent les dégâts à Nabatiyé
france24fr.description: "Nabatiyé est une ville dévastée", déclare Mohammed Salloum, un habitant venu inspecter son magasin endommagé, après qu'Israël a ordonné à ses forces de cesser les combats dans le sud du Liban. "La ville reprendra vie dans deux ou trois mois après cette catastrophe, mais le plus important, c'est que les Israéliens quittent notre terre", déclare M. Salloum.

france24fr.title: Colombie : le candidat de droite De La Espriella remporte la présidentielle
france24fr.description: Le candidat de droite Abelardo De La Espriella a remporté de ⁠justesse l'élection présidentielle rganisée ​dimanche en Colombie, selon un premier décompte des voix, les électeurs ayant misé sur sa promesse, soutenue par Donald Trump, de lutter contre la criminalité et de renforcer l'économie.

france24fr.title: La propagande russe affirme que la "libération" du Donbass est proche
france24fr.description: Volodymyr Zelensky espère que les frappes de drone ukrainiennes contre Moscou feront prendre conscience aux Russes "qu'un seul homme", Vladimir Poutine, mène la guerre. De son côté, la propagande russe justifie sa narration d'une Russie "agressée" par des "nazis". Derrière cette rhétorique, les buts de guerre de Poutine restent inchangés : prendre la région ukrainienne du Donbass et parvenir à un renversement des élites européennes favorables à Kiev. Sa propagande promet toujours aux Russes une

france24fr.title: Canicule : jusqu'à 210 milliards d'euros de pertes pour l'économie française d'ici 2030
france24fr.description: La chaleur extrême n'est plus seulement un enjeu sanitaire ou environnemental. Selon une étude de l'assureur Allianz Trade, elle pourrait devenir un frein à la croissance en France, en pesant sur la productivité, l'investissement et les finances publiques.

france24fr.title: L'UE cherche à contrer la crise énergétique
france24fr.description: Après la crise énergétique provoquée par l’invasion de l’Ukraine, le conflit au Moyen-Orient rappelle le coût économique de la dépendance européenne aux énergies fossiles importées. La flambée des prix menace la croissance et entretient l’inflation. Dans ce contexte, les investissements dans les énergies renouvelables ne répondent plus seulement à des objectifs climatiques : ils sont aussi devenus un enjeu de résilience économique, de compétitivité et d’indépendance stratégique pour l’Europe.

france24fr.title: Andy Burnham, le "roi du Nord" favori pour succéder à Keir Starmer à Downing Street
france24fr.description: Le maire travailliste du Grand Manchester, Andy Burnham, a récemment été élu député avec l'objectif de détrôner Keir Starmer. Il a désormais le champ libre, après l'annonce de la démission du Premier ​ministre britannique, faite mardi. Starmer a déclaré qu'il resterait en poste jusqu'à la désignation de son successeur à la tête du Parti travailliste.

france24fr.title: Congé maternité en Inde : une avancée illusoire
france24fr.description: En 2025, la Cour suprême indienne a déclaré que le congé maternité constitue un droit fondamental pour toutes les femmes actives. L’Inde figure parmi les pays au monde où les femmes ont droit à 26 semaines de congé maternité rémunéré, applicable pour un maximum de deux enfants. Mais il reste encore un long chemin à parcourir pour garantir pleinement les droits des mères actives. Reportage de Navodita Kumari et Zubair Dar, avec Selma Daoui.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Algérie et la Jordanie jouent leur survie
france24fr.description: L'Algérie et la Jordanie s'affrontent mardi matin à San Francisco dans une rencontre qui pourrait être fatale pour le perdant. Les deux équipes ayant perdu leur premier match de poules, contre l'Argentine et l'Autriche respectivement, seuls un nul ou une victoire assureraient la survie dans ce groupe et une opportunité de se qualifier lors du dernier match de la phase de groupe.

france24fr.title: Le Premier ministre britannique Keir Starmer annonce sa démission
En direct : le Premier ministre britannique Keir Starmer annonce sa démission
france24fr.description: Sur la sellette depuis plusieurs semaines, le Premier ministre britannique Keir Starmer a finalement annoncé lundi sa démission. Le Royaume-Uni va donc connaître son septième Premier ministre en dix ans, une instabilité sans précédent dans l'histoire moderne de ce pays. Suivez en dire la situation politique après sa démission.

france24fr.title: La canicule s'amplifie encore en France, 49 départements en vigilance rouge
france24fr.description: Les chaleurs étouffantes qui frappent le pays depuis près d'une semaine "montent d'un cran", lundi, avec 49 départements et 35 millions de Français placés en vigilance rouge canicule par Météo France. Cette situation pousse notamment les autorités à fermer ou à réorganiser près de 2 000 établissements scolaires.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : Lamine Yamal booste l'Espagne, la Belgique encore accrochée
france24fr.description: Après une entrée en lice ratée face au Cap-Vert, l'Espagne a facilement battu l'Arabie saoudite (4-0) grâce au premier but de Lamine Yamal en Coupe du monde et à un doublé d'Oyarzabal.

france24fr.title: Avec Barros à Little Sénégal, où New-York vibre pour les Lions de la  Teranga
france24fr.description: Alors que les Lions sénégalais s’apprêtent à affronter la Norvège, direction Little Sénégal à Harlem avec l'influenceur Barros. Dans ce quartier emblématique de New York, la diaspora sénégalaise fait vivre la Teranga à des milliers de kilomètres de Dakar. Dans les rues animées, les associations et les commerces communautaires, immersion dans ce petit coin de Sénégal qui rêve d'une victoire.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: L'Espagne enfin lancée, la Belgique en danger, le Cap-Vert homérique une fois de plus et la victoire historique de l'Égypte… Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Entre Meloni et Trump, divorce à l'italienne
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce lundi 22 juin, le divorce entre Girogia Meloni et Donald Trump. La démission annoncée du Premier ministre britannique Keir Starmer, presque 10 ans jour jour après le référendum sur le Brexit. Et l’entrée, demain, au Panthéon, de l’historien et résistant Marc Bloch et de son épouse, Simonne Vidal.

zeit.description: Die israelische Armee hat im Westjordanland zwei junge Palästinenser erschossen. Sie sollen zuvor eine israelische Siedlung angegriffen haben.

zeit.description: José Luis Abalos stehen nach einem Gerichtsurteil 24 Jahre in Haft bevor. Es ist das erste Urteil in einer Reihe von Korruptionsvorwürfen gegen Vertraute der Regierung.

zeit.title: Social-Media-Verbot für Kinder: Bündnis spricht sich gegen pauschales Social-Media-Verbot aus
zeit.description: Mehrere Institutionen warnen vor einem generellen Verbot von sozialen Netzwerken für Jugendliche. Diese seien wichtig für die Entwicklung von Kindern.

zeit.title: Kommunale Spitzenverbände: Kommunen kritisieren Einsparungen und fordern Soforthilfe
zeit.description: Städte und Gemeinden erwarten hohe finanzielle Belastungen in Hinblick auf geplante Reformen der Bundesregierung. Der Präsident des Städtetags fordert eine Soforthilfe.

zeit.title: Großbritannien: Britischer Premierminister Keir Starmer kündigt Rücktritt an
zeit.description: Keir Starmer folgt den Forderungen seiner Partei: Er wird zurücktreten. Bis seine Partei einen Nachfolger ernannt hat, bleibt er im Amt.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: US-Vizepräsident JD Vance spricht über die Verhandlungen mit Iran +++ Irans Top-Verhandler unterwegs nach Hause
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Auf dem Bürgenstock wird nun um ein Ende des Konflikts gerungen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Regierungskrise in Grossbritannien: Das Vereinigte Königreich braucht schon wieder einen neuen Premierminister
nzz.description: In London steht ein erneuter Führungswechsel an. Nach den jüngsten Wahlergebnissen und wachsenden Spannungen in der Labour-Partei ist Premierminister Keir Starmer zurückgetreten. Eine Übersicht.

nzz.title: Deutsche Pragmatik für England, Italianità für Brasilien: Ausländische Trainer sind bei der WM die Regel – Weltmeister wurde mit ihnen noch niemand
nzz.description: Immer mehr Länder verpflichten Coaches aus dem Ausland. Die grosse Ausnahme: Deutschland.

nzz.title: Von der Kavalierstour zur Kreuzfahrt: die Meilensteine, die zum Massentourismus führten
nzz.description: Volle Strände, überbuchte Flugzeuge, dichtes Gedränge beim Sightseeing. Die heutige Art des Reisens ist noch jung. Eine verkürzte Geschichte des Reisens.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die jüngsten Entwicklungen des Ukraine-Krieges in Bildern
nzz.description: Die russische Invasion hat Millionen von Ukrainerinnen und Ukrainern in die Flucht getrieben. Während der Abnutzungskrieg unerbittlich weitergeht, droht Kiew durch die aussenpolitische Neuausrichtung von US-Präsident Donald Trump weiter unter Druck zu geraten. Die aktuellen Entwicklungen in Bildern.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Impressionen der Fussball-WM 2026
nzz.description: Drei Gastgeber, 48 Teilnehmer: Vom 11. Juni bis zum 19. Juli findet die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Männer in Mexiko, Kanada und den USA statt. Einblicke in die WM in Bildern.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Der kantonale Ombudsmann Jürg Trachsel erhält eine weitere Amtszeit +++ Wegen der Hitze wird einer der grössten kantonalen Schulsportanlässe abgesagt
nzz.description: Die neusten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: Er verehrt Trump und Milei: Der rechte Hardliner de la Espriella dürfte neuer Präsident Kolumbiens werden
nzz.description: Als Anwalt verteidigte er üble Gangster, nun steht er mit einem harten Law-and-Order-Programm vor dem politischen Triumph: Abelardo de la Espriella kopiert erfolgreich die Rezepte seiner Vorbilder in den USA, Argentinien und El Salvador.

nzz.title: Olympische Winterspiele 2038 in der Schweiz: Bundesrat will 200 Millionen Franken bezahlen, verspricht aber, es gebe keine Defizitgarantie
nzz.description: Trotz Geldsorgen kann der Sportminister Martin Pfister bekanntgeben, dass der Bundesrat die Olympischen Spiele finanziell unterstützen will. Für ein Defizit würden Private geradestehen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Hitzewelle in der Schweiz und Deutschland dauert an – Temperaturen bis 37 Grad kommen auf uns zu
nzz.description: Wo ist es gerade besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf Mensch und Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren, und Bränden in Europa.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - 36 Grad, und es wird noch heisser: Die besten Bilder, um sich abzukühlen
nzz.description: In zwei Schweizer Gemeinden wurden am Sonntag Hitzerekorde für den Juni geknackt: 36,1 Grad in Buchs (AG) und 35,4 Grad in Delsberg (JU). In Frankreich bleiben heute Hunderte von Schulen geschlossen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: TV-Expertin Emma Hayes muss Taktik in einer Art Showküche erklären - Kritik an Sender
spiegel.description: Emma Hayes ist Nationaltrainerin der US-Frauen und macht bei der WM Taktikanalysen – aber nicht in einem normalen Studio. Und: Boris Becker kritisiert Trinkpausen, ausgerechnet als Ex-Tennisprofi. Alles Wichtige zum Turnier.

spiegel.title: Klimawandel in Ozeanien: Tuvalu wehrt sich gegen den Untergang
spiegel.description: Mit dem Anstieg des Meeresspiegels wurde der Pazifikstaat Tuvalu zum Symbol der Erderwärmung. Doch die Bewohner wollen sich mit der ihnen zugedachten Rolle als Klima-Mahnmal nicht abfinden.

spiegel.title: Heilbronn: Drahtseile über illegalen Fahrradweg gespannt – Jäger wegen versuchten Mordes vor Gericht
spiegel.description: Mountainbiker nutzten verbotenerweise einen kleinen Pfad in einem Wald bei Heilbronn. Ein Jagdpächter soll daraufhin Drahtseile gespannt haben, um die Radfahrer zu stoppen. Vor Gericht hat er sich nun verteidigt.

spiegel.title: Strandbad in Halle (Saale): Kein Deutsch, kein Eintritt
spiegel.description: In einem Strandbad in Sachsen-Anhalt gilt nach einem Vorfall: Wer nicht gut genug Deutsch spricht, erhält keinen Einlass. Das soll der Sicherheit dienen und das Personal entlasten.

spiegel.title: Nicole Kidman gratuliert Ex-Mann Keith Urban zum internationalen Vatertag
spiegel.description: Seit rund einem halben Jahr ist die Ehe von Nicole Kidman und Keith Urban geschieden. Jetzt hat die Schauspielerin dem Country-Sänger einen öffentlichen Gruß hinterlassen – und einen anderen Ex-Mann ausgespart.

spiegel.title: Deutschland - rücksichtslose Radfahrer: Rote Ampel? Mir egal!
spiegel.description: Viele Fahrradfahrer missachten selbst einfachste Regeln – auch deshalb passieren viele Unfälle. Das Bild vom »besseren Verkehrsteilnehmer« weisen jüngere Forschungsergebnisse jedenfalls zurück.

spiegel.title: Die Linke: Luigi Pantisano bittet CDU nach »Faschismus«-Vergleich um Entschuldigung
spiegel.description: Der neue Linkenchef Luigi Pantisano hat seinen CDU-AfD-Vergleich nach scharfer Kritik erst relativiert – nun gibt er sich zerknirscht. Zugleich bekräftigt er seine »grundlegende Kritik am Rechtskurs der Union«.

spiegel.title: Wetter: Hitze-Welle in Deutschland - diese Woche könnte es bis zu 40 Grad heiß werden
spiegel.description: Eine Hitzeglocke zieht über Europa und drückt nach Deutschland hinein. Der Deutsche Wetterdienst spricht von Werten weit über 30 Grad. Auch in Europas Urlaubsländern machen die Temperaturen den Menschen zu schaffen.

spiegel.title: Dominikanische Republik: Hunderte fliehen vor Feuer in Luxushotel in Bayahibe
spiegel.description: Im beliebten Küstenort Bayahibe fegen Flammen durch ein Luxushotel, Hunderte müssen fliehen, eine Urlauberin stirbt. Wind und Palmblätter in der Dachkonstruktion könnten das Feuer weiter angefacht haben.

spiegel.title: Magdeburg: Was der Prozess gegen den Todesfahrer den Überlebenden gebracht hat
spiegel.description: Das Landgericht Magdeburg will bald ein Urteil gegen den Amokfahrer vom Weihnachtsmarkt verkünden. Was hat der Prozess den Überlebenden gebracht?

spiegel.title: Österreich: Deutscher verunglückt bei Wanderung in Vorarlberg tödlich
spiegel.description: Ein Deutscher ist auf einer Bergtour im österreichischen Mittelberg ums Leben gekommen. Laut Polizei rutschte der Mann auf dem Rückweg seiner Wanderung aus und stürzte knapp 50 Meter steil bergab.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Hart und trocken – Rasen im Finalstadion sorgt für Diskussionen
spiegel.description: Vinícius Junior findet den Platz schwer bespielbar, für den Franzosen Adrien Rabiot fühlt sich der Untergrund wie Kunstrasen an. Der Rasen in East Rutherford gefällt nicht allen. Nur eine Nation sieht sich im Vorteil.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Fairplay-Ärger um Federico Viñas und Kap Verde
spiegel.description: Als sein Team 1:0 gegen Uruguay führt, zwingt ein Muskelkrampf einen Kap-Verde-Spieler zu Boden. Der Uruguayer Federico Viñas leistet zunächst Erste Hilfe – bis er erkennt, dass sein Team ein Tor erzielen kann.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Donald Trump prophezeite Rücktritt von Keir Starmer - »kläglich versagt«
spiegel.description: Keir Starmer hat seinen Rückzug als britischer Premier angekündigt. Noch vor der Starmer-Rede verabschiedete US-Präsident Trump den Labour-Chef öffentlich.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Keir Starmer legt Labour-Vorsitz nieder und tritt als Premier ab
spiegel.description: Der britische Regierungschef Keir Starmer legt den Vorsitz seiner Labour-Partei nieder. Dies bedeutet, dass er auch sein Amt als Premierminister verlieren wird. Er hat bereits mit König Charles gesprochen.

spiegel.title: Wandlitzer See: Mann fällt von SUP-Board und ertrinkt
spiegel.description: In Brandenburg ist ein 29-Jähriger bei einem Badeunfall ertrunken. In Nordrhein-Westfalen kam ein Mann ums Leben – beim unerlaubten Schwimmen in einem Baggersee.

spiegel.title: Tschechien: Demonstrationen gegen Pläne zur Abschaffung der Rundfunkgebühren
spiegel.description: Die tschechische Regierung stößt mit ihren Plänen zur Abschaffung der Rundfunkgebühren auf Protest. Am Montag reagierten Beschäftigte mit einem Warnstreik. Moderatoren traten demonstrativ in Trauerkleidung vor die Kamera.

spiegel.title: Nebeneinkünfte von Politikern: Wie viel verdient Ihr Bundestagsabgeordneter nebenbei?
spiegel.description: Insgesamt mehr als zehn Millionen Euro haben die Parlamentarier seit Beginn der Wahlperiode neben ihrer politischen Arbeit verdient. Kommen sich Nebenjobs und Volksvertretung in die Quere?

observador.title: As notícias das 12h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Morreu Alan Greenspan, icónico líder da Fed dos EUA
observador.description: Morreu, poucos meses depois de celebrar 100º aniversário, Alan Greenspan, que passou vários anos à frente do banco central mais poderoso do mundo, a Reserva Federal dos EUA.

observador.title: Trump desmentiu visita de Flávio Bolsonaro à Casa Branca?
observador.description: Publicações sugerem que o Presidente dos EUA desmentiu o encontro com o candidato à presidência do Brasil Flávio Bolsonaro, mas tal não aconteceu. Trump e Flávio Bolsonaro reuniram-se a 27 de maio.

observador.title: Vistos para entrar no Japão ficam cinco vezes mais caros
observador.description: Medida entra em vigor a 1 de julho e visto único sobe de 16 para 80 euros. Governo quer alinhar os custos com os dos restantes países do G7 e garante que não haverá impacto imediato no turismo.

observador.title: Dívida pública e privada no país sobe para 876.200 milhões
observador.description: O endividamento do setor público subiu 5.500 mil milhões de euros devido ao agravamento dos investimentos em títulos de dívida pública, alerta o Banco de Portugal.

observador.title: Taxa Euribor cai a três e sobe a seis e a 12 meses
observador.description: Taxa a três meses, que recuou para 2,313%, manteve-se abaixo das taxas a seis (2,631%) e a 12 meses (2,809%). Euribor a seis meses representava 39,56% do 'stock' de empréstimos para habitação própria.

observador.title: Ex-ministro de Pedro Sánchez condenado a mais de 23 anos
observador.description: Antigo "braço direito" de Sánchez, José Luis Ábalos, condenado a 23 anos de prisão. Victor de Aldama e Koldo García foram também acusados de suborno, desvio de dinheiro público e prevaricação.

observador.title: Corpos de treze pessoas encontrados após ataques israelitas
observador.description: Equipas dos centros de Nabatiye e da Defesa Civil Libanesa realizaram operações no domingo para desobstruir as vias da região. Pelo menos 13 corpos foram recuperados.

observador.title: Von der Leyen agradece a Starmer por liderança na guerra
observador.description: Keir Starmer anunciou que se vai demitir da liderança do Partido Trabalhista. "A segurança da Europa e da Ucrânia está mais forte graças a si. Obrigado, caro Keir", agradeceu Ursula Von der Leyen.

observador.title: Meloni desafia Netanyahu na ONU com bandeira da Palestina?
observador.description: Com uma bandeira da Palestina nas ombros e enquanto "mulher e mãe", Meloni teria desafiado Israel na ONU. "Não posso apoiar o assassinato de crianças inocentes", teria dito. É verdade?

observador.title: Andebol. FC Porto junta-se ao Sporting na Liga dos Campeões
observador.description: Com o alargamento de 16 para 24 equipas, os 'dragões' receberam um dos 13 'wild cards' atribuídos pela EHF, enquanto o Sporting, por ser campeão português, já tinha a presença assegurada.

observador.title: Carris inicia a 4 de julho horário de verão com Linhas Mar
observador.description: Com a chegada do verão, regressam as Linhas Mar, um serviço que proporciona "ligações mais rápidas e diretas às zonas balneares". A partir de 15 de junho, todas as linhas passam já a operar.

observador.title: Vivem em Portugal 11,4 milhões, 1,6 milhões são estrangeiros
observador.description: População residente em Portugal em 2025 “foi estimada em 11.424.031 pessoas, o que corresponde a um aumento de 36.809 pessoas relativamente a 2024". 1.597.539 dessas pessoas são estrangeiras.

observador.title: Alcácer do Sal. Corpo de homem desaparecido foi encontrado
observador.description: Corpo do homem, de nacionalidade timorense, foi "encontrado às 7h39 desta segunda-feira, dentro de água". Vítima entrou na barragem com mais duas pessoas e nunca mais foi avistado.

observador.title: Lei Laboral? "A PSU é ainda mais grave", diz Vieira da Silva
observador.description: Para o socialista a iniciativa do Governo foi mal conduzida até a uma "derrota cega". Miguel Corte Real (CH) fala num chumbo normal e F. Negrão (PSD) admite alguma "falta de sentido democrático".

observador.title: 10h. Primeiro-ministro britânico anuncia demissão
observador.description: Keir Starmer anunciou a demissão do cargo de líder do partido trabalhista.  Ainda, ecos do chumbo das alterações à Lei Laboral e diretores Escolares defendem a suspensão de aulas por causa do calor.

observador.title: "Passos Coelho é grande num país de anões"
observador.description: José Eduardo Martins enaltece o desprendimento e sentido de missão de Passos Coelho. O antigo secretário de Estado diz que Chega "não serve" para PSD por não ser confiável para reformas à direita.

observador.title: Número de mortes por Ébola sobe para 254 na RD Congo
observador.description: Autoridades admitem que pode haver muitos mais casos ainda desconhecidos e que o pico do surto ainda está para acontecer no país. Um total de 100 pessoas conseguiu recuperar da doença.

letemps.title: «Notre prison est chaque jour plus exiguë»: en Afghanistan, des femmes arrêtées puis reniées pour être sorties à visage découvert
letemps.description:
Privées d’études, écartées de nombreux emplois et de la plupart des lieux de sociabilité, les Afghanes risquent désormais d’être arrêtées si elles sortent de chez elles. Pour protester, elles ont lancé un boycott. Sans succès

new-sci.description: Archaeologists have discovered traces of a wooden structure built 5000 years ago, 5 kilometres from Stonehenge, which appears to have been an even older monument for marking the summer solstice

new-sci.title: Cervical cancer deaths have plummeted thanks to HPV vaccine
new-sci.description: We already know the vaccine against human papillomavirus, or HPV, greatly reduces infections and cases of cervical cancer, and now we have the first evidence it prevents deaths too

new-sci.title: Chilling the body with drugs could limit brain damage from stroke
new-sci.description: Putting brain cells into a hibernation-like state via drugs that cool down core body temperature may help to preserve them following a stroke

new-sci.title: Oldest known plague outbreak killed hunter-gatherer children
new-sci.description: DNA evidence shows that plague bacteria devastated a community in Siberia more than 5000 years ago, challenging the idea that there were no major disease outbreaks before the advent of farming and large settlements

phys-org.title: Mapping cotton bacterial blight resistance
phys-org.description: Spoorti Gandhadmath carefully placed 3.5-inch (8.9-centimeter) pots on a shelf in a growth chamber. Within seven days of sowing, newly sprouted leaves had fully emerged from each of the carefully selected seeds, representing diverse cotton genotypes.

phys-org.title: New research advances amaranth as a nutritious and high-performing leafy green crop
phys-org.description: Two complementary studies, appearing in HortScience, from Rutgers University are advancing the potential of amaranth (Amaranthus spp.) as a valuable leafy green by combining detailed morphological characterization with evaluations of horticultural performance and nutritional quality. Amaranth is gaining attention as a versatile crop with strong adaptability, rapid growth and high nutritional value.

phys-org.title: Europe sweats through new heat wave, with worse to come
phys-org.description: France banned alcohol in red-alert areas Sunday, Spain and Germany canceled or postponed sports events, and Britain warned of "tropical nights" as Europe sweltered through a heat wave threatening to break June temperature records.

phys-org.title: Algae microbots take aim at bladder cancer
phys-org.description: Tiny algae-based robots guided by magnets could improve bladder cancer treatment by boosting delivery of chemotherapy drugs into tumors, researchers say.

phys-org.title: The giant viruses that orchestrate life in the polar regions
phys-org.description: Viruses play a major role in the functioning of ecosystems. They profoundly influence the dynamics of microbial communities, the flow of matter and global biogeochemical cycles. Yet despite their abundance and ecological importance, many of them have long remained invisible to science.

phys-org.title: El Niño is underway, satellite observations show
phys-org.description: El Niño, characterized by warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific, made its return in June 2026. Observations of sea surface height from the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich satellite that month indicated that the 2026 event was continuing to strengthen.

phys-org.title: Quantum mechanics theory may work without imaginary numbers, new analysis suggests
phys-org.description: Physicists from Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU) have examined a fundamental property of quantum mechanics in collaboration with the German Aerospace Center (DLR). In an article published in the journal Physical Review Letters, they show that this theory does not necessarily need to be formulated with imaginary numbers—real numbers can, in fact, also be used.

phys-org.title: If you're feeling down, maybe don't pet your cat, new study suggests
phys-org.description: You come home after a stressful day and reach out to your cat for a bit of comfort. It hisses. Maybe takes a swipe. Or simply flicks its tail and saunters off without so much as a meow. A dog, by contrast, greets you as though they've just won the lottery.

phys-org.title: Engineered bacterial spores reveal new protein targets for enzymes and vaccines
phys-org.description: A remarkable quality of bioengineering is that scientists can take biological processes honed by millions of years of evolution and use them to efficiently create drugs, chemicals and other products to improve our lives. Now Tufts researchers have found new ways to expand the potential for using bacterial spores as catalysts for chemical reactions, biofuel production or breaking down pollutants.

phys-org.title: Mars-like conditions fail to kill some Earth pathogens, experiments suggest
phys-org.description: Microorganisms from our planet could survive on celestial bodies where water is present, such as Mars. That is the conclusion of Ph.D. candidate Tommaso Zaccaria after experiments with simulated space conditions. Our immune system reacts less effectively to pathogens that have undergone such a simulated space journey. According to his supervisors, his dissertation provides extraterrestrial insights that are also useful on Earth.

phys-org.title: Nanoscale CoAl design delivers 6 GPa strength with 15% plastic strain at room temperature
phys-org.description: Materials engineers have developed the ability to manipulate structure and matter at the nanoscale for solid-state alloys called intermetallics, making it possible to alter their properties for improved performance.

phys-org.title: White roofs and urban parks reduce heat in cities, but do not offset extreme global warming
phys-org.description: The implementation of reflective white roofs and new urban parks can significantly reduce temperatures in cities and decrease population vulnerability to heat waves, although these measures are not sufficient to counteract the projected increase of more than 6°C (11°F) by 2100, according to a recent study led by the Institute of Environmental Science and Technology at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (ICTA-UAB), Spain.

phys-org.title: Modular nanorobot self-assembles, targets cancer cells and cuts viability
phys-org.description: A team at the University of Basel, Switzerland, has developed a versatile nanorobot with propulsion and payload modules. The two reusable modules autonomously self-assemble and could be used in medicine or industry.

phys-org.title: MINDY3: A hub between protein quality control and DNA repair
phys-org.description: Researchers from the MRC Protein Phosphorylation and Ubiquitylation Unit at the University of Dundee, together with collaborators from ETH Zürich, the Malopolska Center of Biotechnology and the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna, report a new link between protein quality control and DNA damage responses. The work centers on MINDY3, a deubiquitinase enzyme, and reveals that it carries a distinctive EF-hand region that acts as a novel ubiquitin-binding domain.

phys-org.title: Well-known planetary nebula's ear-like lobes rewrite its evolutionary timeline
phys-org.description: Using the Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) and the Manchester Echelle Spectrograph (MES), astronomers from Turkey and Mexico have investigated a planetary nebula discovered two centuries ago, known as NGC 6563. Results of the observations, published June 15 in a special issue of Galaxies journal, yield important insights into the morphology and kinematics of this nebula.

phys-org.title: NASA testing advanced capabilities for moon, Mars rovers
phys-org.description: On a bleak stretch of the Colorado Desert in Southern California, a compact four-wheeled rover recently trundled 16 miles (26 kilometers) with minimal intervention from the team of engineers trailing it. Called ERNEST (Exploration Rover for Navigating Extreme Sloped Terrain), this prototype is being used by NASA to advance both robotic autonomy and the ability to traverse challenging landscapes.

phys-org.title: Stress gives bees sharper vision and faster reactions, researchers discover
phys-org.description: Bumblebees see the world differently under stress, processing visual information more sharply and making quicker decisions, new research from Newcastle University reveals.

phys-org.title: Can North America mine enough rare earth elements?
phys-org.description: In the quest to create a robust supply chain of rare earth elements necessary for the clean energy revolution and everyday modern conveniences, North America has enough deposits of sufficient quality to begin looking in its own backyard, according to a University of Michigan study published in Resources, Conservation and Recycling.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.

proj-syn.title: Developing-Country Risk Is Being Mispriced
proj-syn.description: When investors say there are no “bankable” projects in developing economies, they are typically referring less to project quality than to the cost of capital. But the assumptions driving up risk premia are not supported by the evidence, and until this changes, the misallocation of capital will continue to undermine development.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

crunchbase.title: Saas Isn’t Coming Back. Something Much Bigger Is Replacing It
crunchbase.description: The next wave of software will be AI-native, industry-specific platforms, writes guest author Richard de Silva who believes the biggest winners will be vertical AI companies with deep domain expertise, proprietary data and strong customer relationships, as these advantages create durable competitive moats that generic horizontal SaaS products cannot match.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Robotics Startups On Fire As Venture Funding Surges To Record Numbers In 2026
crunchbase.description: Globally, robotics startups have so far raised $18.8 billion in 2026, compared to $15 billion in the full year of 2025. The figure also handily surpasses the $14.1 billion raised in the peak venture funding year of 2021, and we still have more than six months of fundraising left. We use Crunchbase data to see where the funding went.

crunchbase.title: European Investor Seedcamp Closes On $320M Across Two Funds To Back Seed Startups And Reaches $1B AUM
crunchbase.description: Seedcamp, one of Europe’s earliest seed investors, has closed on its 7th fund of $220 million and a select fund 2 of $100 million to invest in winners from the core fund.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: World-Model Startup Odyssey Leads With $310M In Slower Week For Large Deals
crunchbase.description: This week was not an exceptionally busy one for large funding deals, though we saw sizable rounds in a lively mix of sectors ranging from AI to fintech to quantum computing, biotech and cybersecurity.

crunchbase.title: AT&T Ventures’ Head Vikram Taneja On The New Rules of Seed-Stage Defensibility
crunchbase.description: In an interview with Crunchbase News, Vikram Taneja, head of AT&T Ventures, shares why he believes that while AI has drastically lowered the barrier to building software, it has also shifted the definition of seed-stage technical risk.

crunchbase.title: The Boardroom Blind Spot: When Success Hides Disruption
crunchbase.description: Boards should not wait for poor performance before confronting disruptive technologies like AI and quantum computing. Instead, writes guest columnist and strategic adviser Itay Sagie, they should evaluate the cost of inaction, challenge successful business models while they are still thriving, and proactively imagine how a technology-driven competitor could disrupt their company.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: ‘This System Wasn’t Built For Me’: Black Founders Became Investors To Change Venture Capital
crunchbase.description: The consistently low numbers of U.S. venture funding to Black founders led some to turn to investing in an effort to help level the playing field. Crunchbase News talked with two such founders to hear more about their experiences in raising capital and what they’ve learned from investing.

crunchbase.title: I Sold My AI Startup Before Revenue: Here’s What Investors Missed — And Founders Shouldn’t
crunchbase.description: The greatest long-term value in AI will come from companies solving deep technical challenges at the model and infrastructure level rather than application-layer products built on existing AI platforms, writes angel investor Alexander Kardos-Nyheim. In this guest commentary he shares processes and questions he uses to determine the investability of an AI startup.

crunchbase.title: SpaceX Acquires AI Coding Tool Cursor For $60B In Year’s Largest Startup M&A Deal
crunchbase.description: The acquisition of Cursor gives SpaceX a foothold into the enterprise software development market, where AI-assisted coding has taken off and led large companies to significantly pare back their reliance on human engineers.
